thought.text: The bullseye PGDG repo was removed upstream. Let me check whether the pgrouting library can actually run on the bullseye base image despite the version metadata.

reasoning_content:
bullseye-backports is 404 too? Let me check. Actually bullseye-backports might have moved. Let me reconsider.

The main blocker: `postgis/postgis:17-3.5` is bullseye-based, PGDG bullseye repo is gone (EOL), and pgrouting requires libstdc++6>=13.1.

Options:
1. Modify the db Dockerfile to use a newer base image (trixie-based) e.g. `postgis/postgis:17-master` (trixie, pg17.11). This is the cleanest fix.
2. Install a newer libstdc++6 in the bullseye image.

The guide's prerequisites say Docker Compose. The guide says `docker-compose up -d --build`. The build of the db service is part of the documented install. The failure is an external resource (upstream PGDG repo removed). But I should try to work around it since the guide's method 2 (docker compose dev) and method 3 (production) both build the db service the same way.

Actually the task says: "You may perform actions that are reasonably necessary to carry out the installation." And "Do not treat an encountered error as an installation failure if you are able to recover from it and subsequently complete and verify the installation."

Let me think about which approach is least invasive and reliable. The trixie-based `17-master` image works with pgrouting. But "17-master" is a moving tag. Alternatively `17-3.6-alpine` — no pgrouting there.

Hmm, but there's also a consideration: whether I should modify source files at all. Modifying the Dockerfile is reasonable necessary action to complete installation. But ideally I'd avoid it. Let me first try to install libstdc++6 from a newer Debian in the bullseye image. libstdc++6 13.1+ requires GLIBC_2.38? The trixie libstdc++6 depends on libc6 >= 2.38, but bullseye has glibc 2.31. That would break.

bookworm libstdc++6 = 12.2.0-14, still < 13.1. So no go.

What about pgrouting 4.0.1 built for pgdg11 (bullseye, pgrouting--2.6.0? no). Actually pgrouting 3.x version might have lower libstdc++ requirement. Let's check what bullseye originally shipped: `postgresql-17-pgrouting` 3.x? The blseye pgdg repo had pgrouting versions. Let me check other pool dirs. But the pool only lists 4.0.1 and 4.0.2 .debs apparently (the listing was paginated? there might be more). Let me check for older pgrouting versions in the pool.

Actually the pool listing showed only 4.0.1, 4.0.2 for pgrouting. Debian's own bullseye repo might have pgrouting for postgresql-13? Not for 17.

Alternative: use the trixie-based postgis image. The cleanest deterministic option might be `postgis/postgis:17-master`. But is there a stable trixie tag for postgis 17? The tags list didn't show a non-alpine trixie 17 tag besides master. 18-3.6 is trixie but PG18.

Hmm. But wait — maybe simplest workaround: replace the failing apt-get with a source that works, OR just remove the pgrouting dependency. The app does not use pgrouting extension functions (uses networkx). But init.sh does CREATE EXTENSION pgrouting, which would fail migration/init if not installed, causing the db init to fail.

However, I could install pgrouting from the deb by force (ignoring libstdc++ dependency) if the symbols are compatible. Let me test whether the .so actually loads with bullseye's libstdc++6 10.2.1. The GLIBCXX version needed can be inspected. If it needs GLIBCXX_3.4.32 (gcc 13) then it won't load. Let me check with readelf on the extracted so. Earlier commands were odd. Let me retry carefully.

Actually a better approach: install a newer gcc runtime into bullseye — but that's complex.

Let me just test force-installing the deb and see if CREATE EXTENSION works.

Actually the cleanest and most reliable: switch base image to trixie. But 18-3.6 uses PG18, and the app config/tests may be PG17. The init.sh works with any.

Given the guide explicitly says postgis 17 in a Dockerfile, and the upstream repo is broken, I think the right approach for a benchmark is to make the build work. Let me consider using `postgis/postgis:17-master` which is PG17 on trixie with working pgrouting. But "master" tags change; at this moment it's 17.11.

Wait, let me re-examine: is there a possibility to just point apt at the archive? The `bullseye-pgdg` dist was removed. But there is `bullseye-pgdg-snapshot`? We checked: 404. Hmm.

Let me look at whether the apt.postgresql.org still serves bullseye in a different path. The dists listing had no bullseye. So it's truly removed.

Given evidence, the failure is due to an external resource (upstream repository removed). But I can recover by modifying the Dockerfile. The task says report SUCCESS if I complete and verify. Modification is allowed.

Let me first test force install to potentially keep the exact base image.

Let me test extracting and running with ldd inside the container with newer libstdc++ from bookworm? bookworm is 12.2.0 which satisfies >=13.1? No, 12 < 13. Doesn't satisfy.

Let me check GLIBCXX versions required by the .so.

action.command: cd /tmp && cp x/usr/lib/postgresql/17/lib/libpgrouting-4.0.so . && docker run --rm -v /tmp:/t postgis/postgis:17-3.5 bash -c 'ldd /t/libpgrouting-4.0.so 2>&1 | tail -20; echo "=== GLIBCXX required ==="; strings /t/libpgrouting-4.0.so | grep -oE "GLIBCXX_[0-9.]+" | sort -uV | tail -5; echo "=== GLIBC required ==="; strings /t/libpgrouting-4.0.so | grep -oE "GLIBC_[0-9.]+" | sort -uV | tail -3'
